reason: Selected resolver comparisons support membership-plus-signature checks, with important limits on honest over-rejection and semantic correctness.

candidates.title: Resolve tool identity and signature before execution policy
candidates.rule: For raw-JSON or merged MCP tool calls, check the live registry identity and declared argument signature before applying action policy or dispatching the call.
candidates.passage: type-checking is necessary but not sufficient; closed-world membership is the missing primitive.
candidates.finding: In the authors’ benchmark, registry-plus-signature resolution rejects fabricated tools and undeclared arguments that permissive schema or fuzzy-name baselines admit. Qualified server/tool resolution addresses merged MCP namespace ambiguity.
models: Ten hosted-model emission panel; resolver itself deterministic
candidates.conditions: The schema-only baseline is permissive when no tool schema exists; already fail-closed runtimes may have this protection. MCP calls resolve to qualified server/tool pairs.
candidates.limitations: Zero honest over-rejection is a construction check against the resolver’s own generator, not independent validation. Schema-valid borrowed arguments remain semantically ambiguous. Public-split scores and emission counts lack broad seed analysis.
candidates.validation_test: Replay independent honest gold calls and fabricated/ambiguous calls against the actual registry. Measure false rejection, wrong dispatch and semantic tool confusion, including stale schemas and name collisions.

review_scope: Selected abstract, introduction, methods or main-result sections; not a comprehensive paper or appendix review.
